subject: RE: RFP - Redistribution & Commercial Use Rights (Model Catalog)
messages:
From: Michael Chen <mchen@novus.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novus.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP Question: Redistribution & Commercial Use Rights for Models

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the quick onboarding on the RFP portal. We have a few checklist items that require explicit confirmation for our legal and procurement review. Can you confirm the following for models listed in Redwood's public catalog that we may serve from your hosted or private deployments?

1) Redistribution and commercial use: Do your model licenses and attachments permit our downstream redistribution of model outputs to our customers and partners, and do you permit us to include the model artifacts (weights/checkpoints) in a commercial offering if needed?

2) Attribution and notice: Are there required attribution notices or redistribution notices that must accompany generated content or redistributed artifacts?

3) Update notifications & pinning: If a model upstream changes its license or is removed, how are customers notified, and do you provide a mechanism to pin a model version for contractually guaranteed behavior?

4) Contract amendment path: If we need bespoke commercial rights beyond the published license, do you support an amendment process and can you provide standard amendment language?

Please point us to any supporting docs. Attaching the RFP question set for reference.

Appreciate a short answers + attachments so we can close this item with procurement.

Regards,
Michael Chen
Senior Counsel, Novus.ai

Attachments: Novus_RFP_Questions.pdf (application/pdf)
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Subject: RE: RFP Question: Redistribution & Commercial Use Rights for Models

Michael — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by details and attachments.

Short answers (summary):
- Redistribution & commercial use: Depends on the upstream model license. For most curated open models in Redwood's catalog, downstream output may be used commercially. Redistribution of model artifacts (weights) depends on the model's original weight license and we flag models that prohibit redistribution.
- Attribution: Varies by license. Some require a simple attribution statement; others have no requirement. We surface attribution requirements in the model metadata.
- Updates & pinning: We provide pinning at the model-version level (exact hash/commit). Customers can opt into automatic updates or pin indefinitely; we also send update notifications to the account email + console alert.
- Contract amendments: Yes — we support custom commercial rights via an amendment/side letter. I attached our catalog license summary and a starter amendment template.

Details: see attached 'Redwood_Model_Catalog_License_Summary_v1.2.pdf' for a matrix of common open licenses (MIT, Apache 2.0, CC-BY-4.0, various model-specific SHARE/weights licenses) and recommended commercial interpretation. Key operational controls we use:
- Model metadata flags (redistribution_allowed: true/false; outputs_restricted: true/false) surfaced in the API and Console.
- Version pining by digest (sha256) with immutable access controls so a pinned version remains stable even if upstream updates.
- License-change alerts: we run weekly provenance checks and post license-change events to the customer's Console and email; we also create an audit trail with the prior license payload.

Next steps: If you need specific contractual language, I can loop in our legal lead (Neha) and have a short amendment drafted.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: RFP Question: Redistribution & Commercial Use Rights for Models

Team — forwarding Novus' RFP Qs (see thread below). They asked for explicit language around redistribution of outputs and redistribution of model weights. Can you review the attached amendment template and confirm whether the clause below is acceptable for commercial amendments, or if we should propose alternate wording? Want a short, redlined version we can send back tomorrow.

Proposed clause (starter):
"Customer may use model outputs for commercial purposes and incorporate such outputs into Customer's products and services; redistribution of model weight files or checkpoints is permitted only where the upstream model license grants such rights and where Redwood has marked the model as 'redistribution_allowed' in the model metadata. Any redistribution of model artifacts must carry the same attribution and notices required by the upstream license. Redwood will not transfer warranties or liabilities arising from upstream license terms; Customer acknowledges responsibility to comply with upstream license obligations when redistributing artifacts."

Please advise on tightening language re: indemnity, attribution statements, and notification triggers (what constitutes a license change event).

Thanks,
Sean
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Michael Chen <mchen@novus.ai>, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, procurement@novus.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: RFP Question: Redistribution & Commercial Use Rights for Models

Michael — attaching our redlined amendment and a brief FAQ for procurement. High level: we will not grant redistribution of proprietary upstream weights where the upstream license forbids it; where redistribution is permitted by upstream license, Redwood can grant rights by contract (see clause 2.1 in the attached amendment).

Summary of changes / clarifications we included in the redline:
- Explicit definition of "Model Artifacts" and "Model Outputs" to avoid ambiguity.
- Attribution: required only where expressly mandated by the upstream license; we provide suggested attribution text in Appendix A.
- Pinning & Notifications: Customer can pin a model by digest; Redwood will notify via email and Console when provenance checks alter license metadata. Notification triggers: upstream license metadata change, model removal from catalog, or known re-licensing event.
- Indemnity: Redwood disclaims indemnity for upstream license non-compliance; Customer indemnifies Redwood for improper redistribution of artifacts when Customer chooses to redistribute.
- Amendment path: We included a signature block and a quick DocuSign link for expediency.

Doc links and attachments included: 
- Redwood_Model_Catalog_License_Summary_v1.2.pdf
- Redwood_Commercial_Use_Amendment_Template_Redline.docx
- FAQ_for_Procurement.txt

If this looks good I can send the DocuSign request to the Novus signature team.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
